terms.body: Finding how much two numbers make together. The answer is called the sum.
Finding what is left when you take one number away from another, or the difference between two numbers. The answer is called the difference.
Finding the total of several equal groups. The answer is called the product.
Sharing a number into equal groups, or finding how many groups fit. The answer is called the quotient.
The table of all multiplications of the numbers 1 to 9, learned by heart.
In addition, when a place adds up to 10 or more, you add 1 to the next place up.
In subtraction, when a place is too small to subtract from, you take 1 (worth 10) from the next place up.
Writing numbers with their places lined up in columns and calculating from the ones place.
The number left over when a division does not come out even. It is always smaller than the divisor.
In 3×4, both 3 and 4 are factors. Swapping them gives the same answer.
The value a digit has because of where it is, such as ones, tens or hundreds.
A way of writing a calculation with numbers and +, −, × or ÷.
